notes: Iteration 2 tests the new 7-section template (assets/task-template.md). With-skill stayed at 100% (22/22) despite the stricter contract; baseline dropped to 44.6% mostly because the new structural assertions (7 sections, frontmatter, checkbox risks) are stricter.

TBD honesty works: the feature capture used 5 'TBD (needs grilling)' markers rather than inventing scope/acceptance criteria; the bug capture used 2. The chore capture filled all sections with grounded, line-referenced facts and one inline TBD, so zero-marker files are not automatically padded.

Mild solutioning drift in the chore capture: Requirements prescribe batch inserts (inferred, not voiced by the user), though open questions hedge it ('does the runtime even come from inserts?'). Watch this in future iterations; not fixed this round to avoid overfitting.

Baseline contamination caught and corrected: the first iter-2 eval-0 baseline discovered and used the capture-task skill from the project's .claude/skills/ (it is now in the harness skill list). That run was discarded and rerun with skills explicitly off-limits. Future baseline runs for this skill need that guard.

Speed improved vs iteration 1 for with-skill runs (40-55s vs 108-117s) at similar tokens; likely run-to-run variance plus the template removing drafting decisions. Single run per config, so treat as directional.
Eval sandbox artifact: one capture cited the host repo's CLAUDE.md standards inside the fixture project. Harmless here (real usage runs in the real repo), not a skill defect.
